s: The angels worship Allah without pride or weariness and glorify Him night and day. They will welcome the righteous on the promised Day.
The idolaters choose gods beside Allah and worship what cannot benefit or harm them. They and what they worship are described as fuel for hell.
The believers are saved from anguish and benefit from Allah's mercy. Their good works are recorded and not rejected.
The righteous are guided, brought into Allah's mercy, and promised inheritance of the earth. They will be far removed from hell and protected from its sound.
Muhammad is sent as a mercy for the peoples. The peoples are warned to surrender to the One Allah.
Abraham rejects the worship of images and breaks the idols, leaving their chief intact so his people may question it. Allah makes the fire coolness and peace for him and rescues him with Lot.
Lot is rescued from a community that practiced abominations. He is brought into Allah's mercy and counted among the righteous.
Moses is given the Criterion, a light, and a Reminder for those who keep from evil.
Aaron is given the Criterion together with Moses as a light and a Reminder for those who keep from evil.
Noah cries to his Lord, and Allah hears his prayer, saves him and his household from the great affliction, and delivers him from those who denied the revelations.
David gives judgment concerning a field damaged by people's sheep. Allah gives him judgment and knowledge and causes the hills and birds to hymn praise with him.
Solomon is given understanding in the judgment concerning the field. The wind and certain evil ones are subdued to him by Allah's command.
Job cries to his Lord about adversity. Allah hears his prayer, removes his affliction, and restores his household and the like thereof as a mercy.
Dhu'n-Nun cries from the darkness, confessing that there is no Allah save Allah and that he has been a wrong-doer. Allah hears his prayer and saves him from anguish.
Zachariah asks Allah not to leave him childless. Allah hears his prayer, bestows John upon him, and adjusts his wife to bear a child.
She who was chaste is made, together with her son, a token for all peoples after Allah breathes into her something of His Spirit.

l: the son of Mary, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The son of the chaste woman is made a token for all peoples.
The heavens and the earth were once of one piece before Allah parted them. The heavens belong to Allah, and He will roll them up as a recorder rolls up a written scroll.
Allah places firm hills and ravines in the earth and makes it a place where people may find their way. The earth belongs to Him, and the righteous will inherit it.

l: the land which We had blessed, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Abraham and Lot are brought to the land which We had blessed for all peoples. The wind is directed toward it by Solomon's command.
The Scripture is revealed as a Reminder for mankind. It contains the promise that Allah's righteous slaves will inherit the earth.
The Reminder comes from Allah and is rejected by many who turn away. Moses and Aaron are given a Reminder, and the revealed Scripture is described as a blessed Reminder.
The Criterion is given to Moses and Aaron as a means of distinguishing right from wrong, together with a light and a Reminder.
The revelations are denied by evil peoples, for which they are destroyed. Muhammad warns mankind through inspiration.
Inspiration is given to the messengers and tells them that there is no Allah save One Allah. Muhammad is warned and instructed through it.
The idols are images worshipped by Abraham's father and people. Abraham breaks them into fragments except for their chief.
The fire is commanded to be coolness and peace for Abraham. The disbelievers will be unable to repel the fire of punishment.

l: Gog and Magog, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: Gog and Magog will be let loose and hasten out of every mound before the True Promise draws near.
Hell is the destination of the idolaters and what they worship beside Allah. Wailing is their portion there, and they will abide in it.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: On the Day of Resurrection Allah sets a just balance so that no soul is wronged, even by the weight of a mustard seed.
The Hour is feared by those who dread doom. The devout are described as those who fear their Lord and dread the Hour.

l: the True Promise, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The True Promise draws near when Gog and Magog are released and the disbelievers stare in terror.
Every soul must taste death, and no mortal was given immortality before Muhammad.

l: the creation of the heavens and the earth, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The creation of the heavens and the earth was not made in play. Allah created them and all that is between them in truth.
The reckoning of mankind draws near while people remain heedless and turn away from reminders.
Worship belongs to Allah alone, and those in His presence are not too proud or weary to worship Him. The messengers call people to worship Him.
Monotheism is affirmed by the declaration that there is no Allah save One Allah. All messengers were inspired to proclaim this and call people to worship Allah.
Punishment comes upon disbelievers and wrong-doers unexpectedly and cannot be repelled. Those who mock the messengers are eventually surrounded by what they mocked.
Allah's mercy rescues prophets and believers from affliction and brings the righteous into His care. Muhammad is sent as a mercy for the peoples.
Revelation comes from Allah as a Reminder and warning. It tells mankind of His oneness, judgment, punishment, and mercy.
A believer's good works are not rejected. Believers are saved from anguish and share in Allah's mercy.
Prayer is made to Allah in times of distress and need. Allah hears the prayers of Noah, Job, Dhu'n-Nun, and Zachariah and responds to them.
Good deeds are inspired in the prophets and are performed together with worship and alms. Every good work done by a believer is recorded and not rejected.
The balance is set on the Day of Resurrection with justice. No soul is wronged, and even the weight of a mustard seed is brought forward.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 21: The Prophets (Al-Anbiyaa)
s: The Day of Judgment is a day of exact reckoning when deeds are weighed and the promised outcomes of punishment or mercy occur.

Surah 57: The Iron concerns Allah’s sovereignty, knowledge, power, and mercy over creation. It calls people to believe in Allah and Allah's messenger, spend from what they have been entrusted with, and seek forgiveness and the Gardens of Paradise. It contrasts the believers, whose light and rewards are promised, with the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women and the disbelievers, who face separation, loss, and the Fire. It also discusses the sending of messengers, the revelation of scripture and the Balance, iron, the temporary life of the world, and Allah's infinite bounty.

l: Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid), Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: Surah 57: The Iron was revealed at Medina. It teaches Allah’s sovereignty, calls for belief and spending, describes the destinies of believers and disbelievers, and discusses messengers, scripture, iron, and Allah's bounty.

Allah is the Mighty, the Wise, the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and the Knower of all things. He creates, gives life and death, owns the heavens and the earth, sends revelations, forgives, gives mercy, and bestows bounty upon whom He will.
Allah's messenger calls people to believe in their Lord. Believers are instructed to believe in him, and Allah promises those who put faith in him a twofold share of mercy, a light, and forgiveness.

The believers are called to believe in Allah and Allah's messenger, spend in Allah's way, and seek forgiveness. On the Day of Judgment, their light will shine before them and on their right hands, and they will receive the glad news of the Gardens.

l: the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: The hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will ask the believers to share their light on the Day of Judgment. A wall will separate them, with mercy inside and doom outside, and they will be told to seek light elsewhere.

l: the People of the Scripture, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: The People of the Scripture are told that they control none of Allah's bounty. Allah's bounty is in His hand to give to whom He will.
The disbelievers are denied ransom on the Day of Judgment and are assigned the Fire. Those who disbelieve and deny Allah's revelations are described as owners of hell-fire.
The heavens glorify Allah, and Allah owns them. Their breadth is used to describe the Garden promised to those who believe in Allah and His messengers.
The earth glorifies Allah and belongs to Him. Allah knows what enters and emerges from it, and He quickens it after its death.

l: the Gardens of Paradise, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: The Gardens are promised to believers as a supreme triumph. Rivers flow beneath them, and those who enter them remain immortal.
The Fire is the home and patron of the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women and the disbelievers. It is described as a hapless journey's end and as hell-fire.

Light will shine before the believing men and women and on their right hands on the Day of Judgment. The hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will ask to borrow it, but they will be separated from the believers by a wall.
Allah's bounty includes forgiveness, the Gardens, mercy, and rewards for belief and spending. It is in Allah's hand, and He gives it to whom He will; Allah is of Infinite Bounty.
The Scripture was revealed with the messengers together with the Balance so that mankind might observe right measure. Prophethood and scripture were placed among the seed of Noah and Abraham.
Allah revealed iron, in which there is mighty power and many uses for mankind. Its revelation is connected with Allah knowing who helps Him and His messengers though unseen.

l: the life of the world, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: The life of the world is described as play, idle talk, pageantry, boasting, and rivalry in wealth and children. Its attractions are temporary and illusory, like vegetation that dries and becomes straw.
The Hereafter contains grievous punishment as well as forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure. It is presented as the lasting outcome beyond the temporary life of the world.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: On the Day of Judgment, believers will have shining light and receive news of the Gardens. The hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will be separated from them, and no ransom will be accepted from the disbelievers.

l: the sending of messengers, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: Allah sent messengers with clear proofs. Noah, Abraham, and Jesus, son of Mary, are named among those sent, and Allah caused messengers to follow one another.

l: the revelation of scripture, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: Allah revealed scripture with His messengers and also revealed the Balance so that mankind might observe right measure. He sent clear revelations to bring people from darkness into light.

l: the reward for belief and spending, Surah 57: The Iron (Al-Hadid)
s: Those who believe in Allah and Allah's messengers, give alms, and spend in Allah's way receive doubled reward, a rich reward, light, and mercy. Those who spent and fought before the victory have a greater rank than those who did so afterward, though Allah promises good to each.

The unit concerns divorce, the conduct of men and women during the legal waiting period, and duties owed to Allah. Men are instructed to keep women in their houses during the period, provide for them, and either take them back or part from them kindly. Allah promises a way out, provision, ease after hardship, and forgiveness to those who keep their duty to Him. The unit also warns of punishment for communities that revolt against Allah's ordinance and describes believers, Allah's revelations, light, Gardens, the seven heavens, and the earth.
It gives instructions concerning divorce, the legal waiting period, maintenance, reconciliation, and separation. It also warns against disobedience to Allah and describes His power and knowledge.

Allah commands proper conduct in divorce, provides a way out and provision for those who keep their duty to Him, and makes their course easy. Allah has created seven heavens and the earth, is Able to do all things, and surrounds all things in knowledge.
The prophet is addressed with instructions concerning how men should put away women and reckon the legal period. A messenger recites Allah's revelations to bring believers from darkness into light.

Men are instructed to put away women according to their legal period, reckon the period, keep their duty to Allah, provide lodging and maintenance, and either take women back or part from them kindly.

Women who are put away must observe their legal waiting period. They are not to be expelled from their houses or leave them unless they commit open immorality, and pregnant women are to be supported until they give birth.
Divorce is to be conducted according to the legal period, with kindness, upright testimony, and proper provision. Reconciliation or separation is to occur kindly when the term is reached.
The legal waiting period is to be reckoned. It is three months for women who despair of menstruation and those who have it not, while pregnant women's period lasts until they give birth.
Allah's limits include rules about housing, leaving the house, and divorce. Whoever transgresses Allah's limits wrongs his own soul.
Allah appoints a way out for whoever keeps his duty to Him.
Allah provides for those who trust Him from where they do not expect. Men are instructed to spend according to the abundance or measure of their provision.
Allah's command comes to pass, and He has set a measure for all things. His commandment is revealed to people.
Communities that revolt against the ordinance of Allah and His messengers are called to a stern account and punished with dire punishment.
Punishment comes to communities that revolt against Allah's ordinance and His messengers. Allah has prepared stern punishment for them.
Believers are exhorted to keep their duty to Allah. Those who believe and do good works are brought from darkness into light and enter Gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Those who believe and do good works are brought from darkness into light and enter Gardens where they abide forever.
Allah has sent down a reminder to people, consisting of a messenger reciting His revelations.
A messenger recites the revelations of Allah made plain. They bring those who believe and do good works from darkness into light.
Believers who do good works are brought from darkness into light.
Believers who believe and do right are brought into Gardens underneath which rivers flow, where they abide forever.
Allah created seven heavens.
Allah created of the earth the like of the seven heavens.

Surah 76: Man (Al-Insaan) concerns man, his creation, guidance, choices, and ultimate consequences. Allah creates man from a drop of thickened fluid, shows him the way, and prepares differing outcomes for the grateful, the righteous, and the disbelievers. The righteous receive a Garden, fine clothing, pure drink, and acceptance of their endeavour, while disbelievers and evil-doers face punishment. The unit also concerns the Qur'an as a revelation and instructs submission, remembrance, and worship of Allah.
Surah 76: Man (Al-Insaan) describes man's creation, guidance, duties, and final outcomes. It presents Allah's rewards for the righteous and punishment for disbelievers and evil-doers.
Man is created from a drop of thickened fluid and is made hearing and knowing. Man is shown the way and may be grateful or disbelieving; Allah can replace people with others like them.

Allah creates man, shows him the way, prepares manacles, carcans, and a raging fire for disbelievers, and wards evil away from the righteous. Allah rewards those who endure, reveals the Qur'an, is Knower and Wise, and admits whom He wills into His mercy.

The righteous drink from cups mixed with Kafur and Zanjabil and feed the needy, the orphan, and the prisoner for the sake of Allah. Allah wards the evil of the day from them and awards them a Garden, silk attire, joy, and pure drink.
Disbelievers have manacles, carcans, and a raging fire prepared for them. They are also among those whose conduct is opposed by the command to obey Allah rather than any guilty one or disbeliever.
The Qur'an is revealed by Allah as a revelation. The unit instructs the addressed person to submit patiently to Allah's command.
Revelation is identified with Allah's revealing the Qur'an. It is presented as an admonishment through which whoever wills may choose a way unto his Lord.
The Garden is awarded to the righteous for all that they endured. In it they recline on couches, find neither the heat of a sun nor bitter cold, receive clustered fruits, and wear silk attire.
Reward is given to the righteous for what they endured, including a Garden, silk attire, and pure drink. Their endeavour upon earth is said to have found acceptance.
The way is shown to man, who may be grateful or disbelieving. This admonishment allows whoever wills to choose a way unto his Lord, though people do not will unless Allah wills.
Painful doom is prepared for evil-doers. The unit contrasts this doom with Allah's mercy and the rewards given to the righteous.

l: the day of judgment, Surah 76: Man (Al-Insaan)
s: The text refers to a grievous day and a day of frowning and fate that people fear. Allah wards the evil of that day from the righteous, while those who love fleeting life put the remembrance of a grievous day behind them.

l: The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: This unit concerns God’s compassion, worship, charity, fasting, reading the Korān, honest labour, fighting for the faith, judgment, women and slaves, animals, and hospitality. It describes rewards and punishments connected with prayer, almsgiving, conduct, debt, justice, family relations, and treatment of animals. It also records teachings attributed to the Prophet about social duties, religious observance, and ethical behavior.

l: God, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: God is described as compassionate, forgiving, rewarding good deeds, and drawing near to those who approach Him. He loves generosity, purity, liberality, munificence, and good treatment of servants and animals.

l: the Prophet, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: The Prophet teaches about worship, charity, fasting, honest work, warfare, judgment, women, slaves, animals, and hospitality. He gives practical instructions, including feeding the hungry, paying labourers, caring for slaves, and protecting noncombatants.

l: the Devil, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: The Devil ties three knots upon a sleeping person’s neck and urges continued sleep. He also enters a house where God’s name is not remembered and claims lodging there.

l: Muslims, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Muslims are urged to pray, read the Korān, fast moderately, give charity, work honestly, avoid begging and unlawful gain, repay debts, and treat others and animals well. A Muslim who reads the Korān is compared to an orange fruit with pleasant smell and taste.

l: women, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Women are discussed in relation to marriage, virtue, consent, worship, household conduct, and social leadership. Women are encouraged to give alms, and their homes are described as better for them than mosques.

l: slaves, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Slaves are described as brothers whose owners must provide them with food and clothing and not burden them beyond their power. A person who beats or slaps a slave without fault must free the slave, and ill-treatment of a slave prevents entry into Paradise.

l: judges, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Judges must not decide between two people while angry. Just and unjust judges alike face severe accountability before God, while a just judge is described as experiencing great fear on the Day of Resurrection.

l: Paradise, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Paradise is promised in connection with generosity, virtuous conduct, and certain forms of devotion. The liberal person is described as near Paradise, and a woman whose husband is pleased with her is said to enter it.

l: Hell Fire, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Hell Fire is associated with suicide, stinginess, and mistreatment of slaves. A person who kills himself is described as remaining in Hell Fire everlastingly.

l: the Day of Resurrection, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: The Day of Resurrection is presented as a time of judgment, punishment, reward, and divine accountability. Murder is named as the first judgment passed on man, and debts remain serious even for a martyr.

l: prayer, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Prayer is praised as a duty witnessed by angels, and prayers performed in congregation receive double the reward of those said at home. Missed prayers are to be performed when remembered, and prayer is connected with ablution, purity, and charity.

l: charity, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Charity includes almsgiving, justice between people, helping riders and their baggage, kind speech, assisting questioners, walking toward prayer, and removing harmful objects. Giving secretly is highly praised, and generosity is described as bringing God’s pleasure and the friendship of people.

l: fasting, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Fasting is not considered complete when a person continues lying and slandering. The unit recommends moderation, including fasting three days each month while also resting, eating, and fulfilling duties to the body, eyes, wife, visitors, and guests.

l: the Korān, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Reading the Korān is compared to possessing the pleasant qualities of an orange or sweet basil, depending on the reader’s character. It should be read constantly because it is said to run away faster than an untethered camel.

l: labour and profit, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Honest labour and earnings are praised, especially work performed by a person or his children. Begging is discouraged, while truthful trade, avoiding interest and monopoly, relieving debtors, and paying labourers promptly are commanded.

l: fighting for the faith, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Fighting for the faith is described as better than worldly life and prolonged supererogatory prayer. The Prophet instructs armies not to kill old men unable to fight, children, or women, not to steal spoils, and to maintain good relations.

l: judgment, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Judgment includes accountability for murder, suicide, debt, and the conduct of judges. A judge who rules between people is described as being held by the neck before God’s court on the Day of Resurrection.

l: hospitality, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Hospitality requires respecting guests, being kind for one day and one night, entertaining them for three days, and not allowing a guest to remain long enough to inconvenience the host. Remembering God when entering the house and eating prevents the Devil from claiming the house and meal.

l: animals, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: Animals must be treated with care, ridden only when fit, and allowed to rest when tired. Good deeds toward animals, including giving them water, are rewarded, and a woman is described as forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog.

l: debt, The Table-Talk of the Prophet Mohammad (Part 1)
s: People who owe debts should be given additional time, and forgiving part or all of a debt is praised. Debt is described as so serious that a martyr is forgiven every fault except debt, and refusing to pay when able warrants dishonour and punishment.
